claims.text: **Chemistry insight:** The near-equimolar density of ~831 kg/m³ lies between the pure-component values of ~781 kg/m³ (propan-2-ol) and ~997 kg/m³ (water) at 298.15 K. The propan-2-ol + water system is well known for exhibiting significant negative excess volume — the mixture is denser than ideal (volume-additive) mixing would predict. This arises because propan-2-ol molecules partially disrupt water's tetrahedral hydrogen-bond network, allowing more efficient molecular packing in the mixed state.
claims.reason: Correct component ordering and accepted negative-excess-volume/hydrogen-bond packing explanation; composition-window mean is already separately assessed.

evidence.assessment: Correct component ordering and accepted negative-excess-volume/hydrogen-bond packing explanation; composition-window mean is already separately assessed.
